drafted_from: tool:read-a-mail-draft's own row in tools/read-and-write-mail/tool-rows.json and the neutral rows of read-data/neutral.mjs; the answer is the shape the Gmail adapter and the stand-in test of test/mail-adapters.test.mjs produce for this sample input
start_here: Say to your AI: "Read my draft r-7301442210. Use my Gmail account connection service_connection:google-account:sam-bakery." It runs tool:read-a-mail-draft as that account on the provider gmail and hands back the neutral row.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: it calls the mail provider for one account the connection names and answers the neutral row.
instructions: 1. Connect your mail account in your Workshop connections and note its handle, like service_connection:google-account:sam-bakery; the provider is the id in read-data/mail-providers.json that account is on (gmail for it).

2. Say to your AI: "Read my draft r-7301442210." and let it call run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:read-a-mail-draft and the input {"provider":"gmail","connection":{"connection_id":"service_connection:google-account:sam-bakery"},"draft_id":"r-7301442210"}.
3. Read what comes back: the draft as a neutral message, needs_original says whether a plain-text edit would lose anything.
4. A provider that does not offer the job says so in words and nothing is sent.
